main_statement.latex: Fix any Grothendieck coherator C. Let X be a cellular C-infinity-groupoid, let n>=0, and let a:D_n->X be any cell. In the pushout square [D_n --s_n--> D_{n+1}; a down; X --i--> X^+] where s_n is the source inclusion, the map i:X->X^+ is a weak equivalence.
main_statement.paraphrase: Henry's pushout conjecture (Henry 2016 Conj 5.3.3): freely adjoining to a cellular weak globular infinity-groupoid a new n-cell a' parallel to an existing n-cell a together with an (n+1)-cell a -> a' (an 'elementary expansion') does not change pi_0 or any based homotopy group, even though the free algebraic construction creates many new composites and coherence cells. By Henry's reduction this yields the canonical left semi-model structure and a Quillen equivalence with spaces (the homotopy hypothesis) for every coherator in the Ara-Henry convention.

comparator.theorem: OAI.Grothendieck.elementary_expansion (C : GlobularTheory) (hC : C.IsCoherator) (X : C.Model) (hX : X.IsCellular) (n : N) (a : disk C n --> X) (Y : C.Model) (i : X --> Y) (b : disk C (n+1) --> Y) (square : IsPushout a (J C n) i b) : WeakEquivalence hC i
comparator.model: Self-contained encoding (comparator re-declares all definitions; solution Model.lean matches them verbatim up to namespace placement). GlobularSet: Cell : N -> Type, source/target with globular identities. Globe category with Face (id | face lt side). Table/Shape: iterated pushouts in presheaves on Globe (Type 0) gluing d_h to the target b-face of the last globe, b < last, b < h; Hom of Shape = presheaf maps (Theta_0 full subcategory). TheoryData: category on Shapes with base functor; GlobularTheory: base preserves the designated pushouts. AdmissiblePair: (n, arity S with height <= n+1, parallel source/target : globe n -> S). IsFreeExtension: universal property among GlobularTheories under base. CellularPresentation: N-indexed tower, stage 0 initial, each step a free extension by fillers of admissible pairs, colimit universal property. IsCoherator: such a presentation exists AND every admissible pair has a filler. Model: presheaf on C.Obj taking designated pushouts to pullbacks. disk n = yoneda(globe n); J n = yoneda(source n). Model.IsCellular: transfinite composition (well-ordered, OrderBot, SuccOrder) from an initial model whose successor steps are BoundaryAttachments (universal property of attaching a family of cells along boundaries). WeakEquivalence hC f: componentsMap bijective (Quot of Joined 0) and for all x : 0-cell, n, homotopyMap bijective, where HomotopyGroup x n = (n+1)-cells with source = target = baseCell x n (iterated chosen unit C.unit := Classical.choose of a filler of the pair (id,id)) modulo Joined (n+1). IsPushout is taken in the category C.Model (models of the theory), as in the paper.

main_statement.match_check: Exact for Theorem 1.1. (i) Coherator: generators d_j -> S adjoined for parallel pairs d_{j-1} => S with dim(S) <= j matches AdmissiblePair (filler dimension n+1, arity height <= n+1); condition (2) matches IsCoherator.2; 'freeness includes globular completion' matches IsFreeExtension quantifying over GlobularTheories. (ii) Cellular = transfinite composite of boundary attachments (paper: pushouts of coproducts of I_j, including I_0). (iii) J_n = source inclusion D_n -> D_{n+1}; the square is a pushout in Mod(C). (iv) W = bijection on pi_0 and on pi_r(X,x) for r>=1 at all vertices x, with based groups at iterated units: matches Components/HomotopyGroup with the chosen unit. Group structure is not part of the statement (bijection of sets), but HomotopyGroups.lean upgrades it to MulEquiv (homotopyGroupIsoOfWeakEquivalence), so nothing is lost. (v) Universe: shapes live in Type 0, theories/models in Type v; harmless.
main_statement.formalized_vs_claimed: Formalized: Theorem 1.1 (= Henry's pushout conjecture) for all coherators in the Ara-Henry convention, arbitrary (transfinite) cellular X and arbitrary attaching cell. NOT formalized: Cor 5.1 (semi-model structure), Cor 5.2 (Quillen equivalence with spaces = the homotopy hypothesis of the title), Prop 2.4 directions (1)=>(2)=>(3), Lemmas 2.2-2.3 (division, change of boundary), Lemma 2.5 (2-out-of-3 etc. for W). The title claim therefore rests on Theorem 1.1 (Lean) + Henry 2016's reduction (Thm 5.1.2(5), Prop 5.3.6-5.3.7, Cor 5.3.12-5.3.13; an arXiv preprint) + the paper's spelled-out verification of Henry's hypotheses (unformalized).

proof_architecture.claim: Algebraic setup: coherator tower in free order, models as globular sets with operations, free models D_j, I_j, J_j, cellular objects.

Homotopy calculus and exact-boundary test: weak equivalence <=> every specified boundary lift exists up to one higher cell; closure properties; I-inj = W cap J-inj; unit retractions of J_j. (Lean: only test (3)=>(1) and contractibility tools.)
Coskeletal cutoff R_q (interpreting generators in the original free order; uses arity bound) preserving cells through q; higher attachments preserve lower cells.
Spines T_m(S) reduce free shapes to height m+1 arities; free shapes contractible.
Fix q; descending induction on n; top case E(q,q) by retraction + unique fillers; upper J-cellular maps are in W and upper I-cellular weak equivalences split and are stable under cellular pushout.
Using only higher-index expansions: tree diagrams and whiskered shapes are contractible (compare tree with string; promote edge homotopies via J_{n+1} duplication).
Index-n partial cylinders P_j (stationary below n, one (n+1)-cell at n, upper small-object completion above); skeletal gluing from whiskered shapes shows all P_j, A_j^eps, P(S) contractible.
Partial path functor P on A_q: interpret every generator in free order using contractibility of P(S); endpoints lift all I_j; jointly they lift J_n (tree B).
Endpoint section + unit retraction: iu is a retract of v=i u r in W, so i in W; this closes the descending induction at fixed q.
Remove the cutoff: each exact-boundary test in dimension k is detected in A_q for q >= max(n+1,k+1); hence Theorem 1.1.
Corollaries via Henry 2016: semi-model structure and Quillen equivalence with spaces (homotopy hypothesis).

route_differences_from_paper: Induction invariant: Lean proves ExpansionContraction q r ('J_{>=r}-cofibrations from cofibrant contractible objects have contractible targets') by strong induction on q-r, instead of the paper's E(q,n) ('J_n pushouts from any cellular object are weak equivalences'). Weak equivalence appears only in the final step, which uses CutoffPathData directly for an arbitrary cellular X.

No W calculus: the Lean never proves 2-out-of-3, Lemma 2.2 (division), Lemma 2.3 (change of boundary) or Prop 2.4 (1)=>(3); it uses ExactBoundaryTest, HasFillers, retract closure of HasFillers, and weakEquivalence_of_exactBoundaryTest ((3)=>(1)).

Trees: only whisker-shaped trees (uniform orientation, and ReverseWhisker) on linearized shapes are formalized (Tree.lean, SpineWhisker.lean, ReverseWhisker.lean). The J_{n+1}-duplication argument (Q, a_0, a_1, r, h) is replaced by free_hasFillers_of_top_homotopy: factor g: L -> F(S) by the J_{>=n+1} small object argument, get a contractible Z by the IH, lift generators into Z with lift_of_top_joined, so F(S) is a retract of Z.

Joint endpoint lifting: instead of the 4-vertex tree B, GlobularFrame.criticalJoint_retract (CriticalJoint.lean:13) exhibits the joint-source domain as a retract of the one-sided domain at n+1; CutoffPathData requires joint lifting of J_k for all k >= r (needed because the IH covers the whole class).

Operation interpretation: cylinderTheory = representedTheory (a globular theory of pairs (operation, cylinder map) compatible with endpoints), with a section of cylinderProjection built from the CellularPresentation (the paper's 'interpret in free order'); fullCylinder is then a model, reflected into A_q (reflectedCylinder).
Cofibrant (llp against I-injectives in A_q) is used instead of 'cellular' inside the induction; isCellular_cutoff_cofibrant converts.

eureka_candidates.for: Henry's conjecture was open since 2016 (Lanari's full path object stalled on interpreting all higher operations; Henry-Lanari and Lanari only reached dimension 3; Taylor 2026 still assumes a generalized form). The fix is non-analytic: neither the cutoff, nor 'partial' cylinders stationary below n, nor the downward order occur in the goal or in L. Once in place, contractibility of P(S) makes the interpretation of every operation automatic, and the theorem follows by a retract argument. In Lean the partial path object (cylinderPathData) dominates 65% of the proof DAG and the whisker contractibility another 27%.
eureka_candidates.against: All ingredients are precedented: cylinders as path objects (Metayer; Lafont-Metayer-Worytkiewicz; Lanari 2020 Defs 5.2-6.1, which the paper cites as its strategy), coskeletal truncation (Henry-Lanari 2023 Sec 2), interpretation via endomorphism theories (Ara, Bourke 2016), 'path object with lifting => trivial cofibration' (Brown/Quillen folklore, Henry 2016). The descending induction is an 'add a parameter' IH template (capped at N2 alone). Novelty lies in the combination and the induction order; the device is tailored to this conjecture, so a downstream speedup outside the pushout-lemma family (e.g. (infinity,n)-categories, other coherator conventions, Taylor's controlled theories) is the real test.

correctness_audit.verdict: Theorem 1.1 (Henry's pushout conjecture) is backed by a sorry-free, axiom-clean Lean proof with a faithful, self-contained statement (pending the orchestrator's build + comparator run). The Lean follows a related but leaner route, which independently corroborates the core idea (partial cylinders + descending cutoff induction). The title claim (homotopy hypothesis) is NOT formalized; it rests on Henry 2016's reduction plus the paper's unformalized Section 5 verification. Scope is the Ara-Henry convention of coherators. Unreviewed; no expert reaction found.
